evidence.note: Immediately after the first successful build, measured binary size and noted it as 5.6MB 'well under the 40MB limit' — the binary-size tripwire checked at least once.
Re-measured binary size across subsequent builds and in final verification (5.7MB), so the size constraint was monitored repeatedly, not just once.

Read the reference jobs runner and migrations and implemented job processing with retry/backoff — aligned the job table from the reference at design time, but no test of BEGIN IMMEDIATE claim semantics or cross-runtime execution under the shared DB anywhere in the trajectory.
No mention of latency/p99 benchmarking at any point, and no explicit verification of the no-Ruby-runtime / no-bridge-crate constraint (only implicitly satisfied by using axum/rusqlite).

reasoning: The agent measured the binary size at least once and kept re-checking it across builds, avoided obvious Ruby-bridge crates implicitly, and aligned its job table from the reference migrations — matching the level-5 anchor ('checks the main constraints at least once ... aligns the job table before considering done'). It falls short of level 8 because it never verified the job-queue claim/schema semantics against the reference under the shared DB and never monitored latency (a tripwire it ignored entirely). The repeated binary-size checks push it to a solid rather than borderline 5, but the untested cross-runtime claim semantics and total absence of latency verification keep it below 6-7.
